planner-fingerprint.sql:
select true as ok,
       (waiting.n > 0) as blocked,
       'ap=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(p.updated_at) from public.assignment_progress p) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',rp=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(q.updated_at) from public.reading_progress q) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',n=' || (select count(*) from public.assignments a)::text
       || ',apn=' || (select count(*) from public.assignment_progress p)::text
       || ',rpn=' || (select count(*) from public.reading_progress q)::text
       || ',at=' || to_char(now() at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as fingerprint,
       waiting.n as requests_open_now, waiting.first_id as first_open_request_id, stale.n as stale_claims,
       r.id as newest_request_id, r.kind as newest_request_kind, r.state as newest_request_state,
       r.created_at as newest_request_created_at, r.claimed_at as newest_request_claimed_at,
       r.finished_at as newest_request_finished_at
  from (select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id
          from public.agent_requests g
         where g.state in ('queued', 'claimed')
           and coalesce(g.claimed_at, g.created_at) >= now() - interval '6 hours') waiting
 cross join (select count(*)::integer as n
               from public.agent_requests g
              where g.state in ('queued', 'claimed')
                and coalesce(g.claimed_at, g.created_at) < now() - interval '6 hours') stale
  left join lateral (select g.id, g.kind, g.state, g.created_at, g.claimed_at, g.finished_at
                       from public.agent_requests g
                      order by g.id desc
                      limit 1) r on true
planner-fingerprint.expect: One row: a reading, with one check. fingerprint holds, as one string, the newest assignment_progress and reading_progress change, the count of assignments, the count of assignment_progress rows (apn), the count of reading_progress rows (rpn) and the time of this read. blocked when an agent_requests row is queued or claimed now (filed or taken within the last 6 hours): a sync or an Inbox apply is waiting or running, so the run stops here, before it has stopped a container or spent a question, and is repeated once that request has ended. A request left queued or claimed for more than 6 hours is not a running sync: it blocks nothing and is counted in stale_claims. The last columns are the newest agent_requests row.

planner-unchanged.sql:
with given as (
  select substring($1::text from '^(.*),at=') as planner,
         substring($1::text from ',at=(.*)$')::timestamptz as since
), seen as (
  select 'ap=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(p.updated_at) from public.assignment_progress p) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',rp=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(q.updated_at) from public.reading_progress q) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',n=' || (select count(*) from public.assignments a)::text
       || ',apn=' || (select count(*) from public.assignment_progress p)::text
       || ',rpn=' || (select count(*) from public.reading_progress q)::text as planner
), moved as (
  select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id, max(g.id) as last_id
    from public.agent_requests g, given
   where g.created_at >= given.since or g.claimed_at >= given.since or g.finished_at >= given.since
), running as (
  select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id
    from public.agent_requests g
   where g.state = 'claimed' and g.claimed_at >= now() - interval '6 hours'
), stale as (
  select count(*)::integer as n
    from public.agent_requests g
   where g.state = 'claimed' and g.claimed_at < now() - interval '6 hours'
)
select (seen.planner = given.planner) as ok,
       (seen.planner <> given.planner and (moved.n > 0 or running.n > 0)) as blocked,
       $1::text as planner_before,
       seen.planner || ',at=' || to_char(now() at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as planner_now,
       given.since as since, now() as read_at,
       moved.n as requests_in_window, moved.first_id as first_request_id, moved.last_id as last_request_id,
       running.n as requests_claimed_now, running.first_id as first_claimed_request_id, stale.n as stale_claims
  from given, seen, moved, running, stale
planner-unchanged.expect: One row. ok when the five planner values read the same as in the fingerprint: a row changed, added or deleted in assignment_progress or reading_progress, or an assignment added or removed, makes them differ. A planner that reads the same passes whatever else ran: what did not change was changed by nobody. blocked only when the values differ AND a sync or an Inbox apply could be why: an agent_requests row was created, claimed or finished at or after the time the fingerprint was read, or one was claimed within the last 6 hours and has not ended. Then the change cannot be laid at the Workspace and the run is repeated. A claim older than 6 hours is not a running sync (stale_claims counts them) and does not turn a failure into a repeat.

turn-found.sql:
select (r.state = 'done' and r.error_code is null
        and r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
        and u.id is not null and md5(u.content) = $3::text
        and ($4::bigint is null or r.id > $4::bigint)
        and t.request_id is not null
        and m.id is not null and m.provider = 'claude-cli' and m.finished and m.error_code is null
        and t.retrieval_state = 'found' and t.found_n >= 1 and t.passages_n >= 1 and s.auto_materials >= 1) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       $2::timestamptz as run_started_at,
       (r.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') as asked_in_this_run,
       (md5(u.content) = $3::text) as question_matches,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier as message_tier, m.provider, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code,
       t.tier as turn_tier, t.depth, t.plan_state, t.retrieval_state, t.found_n, t.passages_n, t.memory_n, t.feed_rows,
       t.plan_ms, t.retrieval_ms,
       s.sources_n, s.auto_materials, s.auto_uploads, s.feeds, s.content_sources
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
  left join public.workspace_turns t on t.request_id = r.id
 cross join lateral (select count(*)::integer as sources_n,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.origin = 'auto' and x.kind = 'material'))::integer as auto_materials,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.origin = 'auto' and x.kind = 'upload'))::integer as auto_uploads,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.kind = 'feed'))::integer as feeds,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.kind in ('material', 'upload', 'memory')))::integer as content_sources
                       from public.workspace_sources x
                      where x.request_id = r.id) s
 where r.id = $1::bigint

       (z.state = 'cancelled' and z.error_code = 'cancelled') as earlier_was_stopped, (z.conversation_id = r.conversation_id) as same_conversation, (r.id > z.id) as asked_after_the_stop
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
  left join public.workspace_turns t on t.request_id = r.id
  left join public.workspace_requests z on z.id = $4::bigint
 cross join lateral (select count(*)::integer as sources_n,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.origin = 'auto' and x.kind = 'material'))::integer as auto_materials,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.origin = 'auto' and x.kind = 'upload'))::integer as auto_uploads,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.kind = 'feed'))::integer as feeds,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.kind in ('material', 'upload', 'memory')))::integer as content_sources
                       from public.workspace_sources x
                      where x.request_id = r.id) s
 where r.id = $1::bigint

  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages u on u.id = r.user_message_id and u.role = 'user'

  left join public.workspace_turns t on t.request_id = r.id

 cross join lateral (select count(*)::integer as sources_n,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.origin = 'auto' and x.kind = 'material'))::integer as auto_materials,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.origin = 'auto' and x.kind = 'upload'))::integer as auto_uploads,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.kind = 'feed'))::integer as feeds,
                            (count(*) filter (where x.kind in ('material', 'upload', 'memory')))::integer as content_sources
                       from public.workspace_sources x
                      where x.request_id = r.id) s
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn-upload-found.expect: One row. ok when the request is this run's (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started), its question is the one the step asks (the md5 of the user message's text is the md5 given), it is done with no error code, its answer was written by provider claude-cli and is finished with no error code, and its turn row is stored, and the answer drew on the run's synthetic file: the document given is an upload in state indexed, and the sources hold a row of kind upload and origin auto that names that document.

upload-indexed.sql:
with given as (
  select encode(sha256(convert_to('Marrowbrook archive lamp memo for an acceptance run. The quillfern lamp of the Marrowbrook archive has seven brass hinges and one green shade. Run mark: ' || $1::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') as hash
)
select (count(d.id) = 1
        and count(*) filter (where d.id = $3::bigint and d.state = 'indexed'
                               and d.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') = 1) as ok,
       given.hash as sha256,
       count(d.id)::integer as rows_holding_it,
       min(d.id) as document_id,
       min(d.state) as document_state,
       min(d.error_code) as document_error_code,
       min(d.attempts) as attempts,
       $3::bigint as document_asked_for,
       coalesce(bool_or(d.created_at >= $2::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'), false) as made_in_this_run
  from given
  left join public.workspace_documents d on d.kind = 'upload' and d.sha256 = given.hash
 group by given.hash
upload-indexed.expect: One row. ok when exactly one upload row holds the hash of this run's synthetic file, that row is the document the step noted, it is in state indexed, and it was made in this run (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started). The hash is made here, in the statement, from the nonce the test drew for the run and the fixed words it wrote (the carry-over crosses ids and times and no hash); it is a hash no earlier run used. The host reads this one with db.proofUntil, up to 10 times, 10 seconds apart, while the ingest worker reads and embeds the file. No counter of the status view is compared.

upload-one-row.sql:
with given as (
  select encode(sha256(convert_to('Marrowbrook archive lamp memo for an acceptance run. The quillfern lamp of the Marrowbrook archive has seven brass hinges and one green shade. Run mark: ' || $1::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') as hash
)
select (count(d.id) = 1
        and count(*) filter (where d.id = $2::bigint and d.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds') = 1) as ok,
       given.hash as sha256,
       count(d.id)::integer as rows_holding_it,
       min(d.id) as document_id,
       min(d.state) as document_state,
       $2::bigint as document_asked_for,
       coalesce(bool_or(d.created_at >= $3::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'), false) as made_in_this_run
  from given
  left join public.workspace_documents d on d.kind = 'upload' and d.sha256 = given.hash
 group by given.hash
upload-one-row.expect: One row. ok when, after the file was sent a second time, exactly one upload row holds the hash of this run's synthetic file, that row is the document the first send noted, and it was made in this run. The second send uploaded nothing and found the row; two rows are impossible (a unique index on the hash), so a second row would mean the first send's document is not the one that holds it.

upload-gone.sql:
with given as (
  select encode(sha256(convert_to('Marrowbrook archive lamp memo for an acceptance run. The quillfern lamp of the Marrowbrook archive has seven brass hinges and one green shade. Run mark: ' || $1::text, 'UTF8')), 'hex') as hash
)
select (not exists (select 1 from public.workspace_documents d where d.sha256 = given.hash)
        and not exists (select 1 from public.workspace_documents e where e.id = $2::bigint)) as ok,
       given.hash as sha256,
       (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents d where d.sha256 = given.hash)::integer as rows_holding_it,
       (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents e where e.id = $2::bigint)::integer as rows_with_the_id,
       (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents f where f.kind = 'upload' and f.state = 'deleting')::integer as uploads_deleting_now
  from given
upload-gone.expect: One row. ok when, after the delete, no row holds the hash of this run's synthetic file and no row has the document's id: the row did not stay in state deleting, it was dropped by the second call. uploads_deleting_now counts every upload in state deleting and is a reading, not a condition: a row left by another, stopped run is not this run's to fix.

conversations-unarchived.sql:
select (count(*) >= $2::integer and count(*) filter (where not c.archived) = 0) as ok,
       count(*)::integer as made_in_this_run,
       $2::integer as at_least,
       (count(*) filter (where not c.archived))::integer as listed,
       coalesce(array_agg(c.id) filter (where not c.archived), '{}') as not_archived
  from public.workspace_conversations c
 where c.created_at >= $1::timestamptz - interval '60 seconds'
conversations-unarchived.expect: One row. ok when at least min_conversations conversations were made in this run (created no earlier than 60 seconds before the run started) and none of them is still listed: each step archived the conversation it opened, through the page, and the pack leaves nothing in his list or his memory. not_archived lists the ids still listed.

store-counts.sql:
select (s.course_units_indexed + s.course_units_waiting = (select count(*) from public.bb_file_text)
        and s.course_units_indexed = (select count(distinct e.text_id) from public.bb_text_embeddings e)
        and s.uploads_indexed = (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents d where d.kind = 'upload' and d.state = 'indexed')
        and s.memory_indexed = (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents d where d.kind = 'memory' and d.state = 'indexed')
        and (select count(*)
               from public.workspace_document_text t
               join public.workspace_documents d on d.id = t.document_id
              where d.state = 'indexed'
                and not exists (select 1 from public.workspace_text_embeddings e where e.text_id = t.id)) = 0) as ok,
       (s.course_units_indexed + s.course_units_waiting = (select count(*) from public.bb_file_text)) as course_ok,
       (s.course_units_indexed = (select count(distinct e.text_id) from public.bb_text_embeddings e)) as course_vectors_ok,
       (s.uploads_indexed = (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents d where d.kind = 'upload' and d.state = 'indexed')) as uploads_ok,
       (s.memory_indexed = (select count(*) from public.workspace_documents d where d.kind = 'memory' and d.state = 'indexed')) as memory_ok,
       ((select count(*)
           from public.workspace_document_text t
           join public.workspace_documents d on d.id = t.document_id
          where d.state = 'indexed'
            and not exists (select 1 from public.workspace_text_embeddings e where e.text_id = t.id)) = 0) as none_indexed_without_a_vector,
       s.course_units_indexed, s.course_units_waiting, s.uploads_indexed, s.memory_indexed
  from public.v_workspace_index_status s
store-counts.expect: One row. Task 49's proof 6, whole. ok when the status view's counts agree with a direct count taken in the same statement: course units indexed plus waiting equal the course units; course units indexed equal the distinct course units that hold a vector; uploads indexed and memory items indexed equal the rows of those kinds in state indexed; and no document in state indexed has a unit without a vector. A count is compared only with the direct count of the same statement, never with a count taken at another moment of the run, which an upload of his own would move. The figures are in the detail.
